tier_reason: The pg_jitter v18 page (generated by tests/bench_comprehensive.sh, public) times pg_jitter's sljit backend against PostgreSQL's llvmjit and the interpreter on an Apple M1 Pro, but compiler and build flags are not stated and it does not say whether upstream sljit or the patched vladich/sljit fork was built, so not A. The measurement comes from pg_jitter's own first-party suite (210 stars, not a well-known independent benchmark) and it measures the integration rather than sljit alone, so not B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: pg_jitter benchmark page (https://github.com/vladich/pg_jitter/blob/master/bench/ARM64/0.3.0/BENCHMARKS_v18.md), JIT compilation overhead table: SUM_int llvmjit 22.263 ms vs sljit 0.052 ms, GroupBy_5agg 45.5 ms vs 0.069 ms, Wide1K_groupby 2043.286 ms vs 0.071 ms (about 220x to 29,000x less compile time across 106 queries, median about 480x, derived from page data). End-to-end query time with thresholds forced to 0: SUM_int llvmjit 68.090 ms vs sljit 42.401 ms (interpreter 44.859 ms); GroupBy_5agg llvmjit 149.033 ms vs sljit 99.530 ms (interpreter 117.367 ms); sljit beats llvmjit's total time on 106 of 108 queries (derived from page data). README (https://github.com/vladich/pg_jitter): sljit compile 'tens to low hundreds of microseconds' vs LLVM 'tens to hundreds of milliseconds'. The README's 'sljit is the most consistent: 5-25% faster than the interpreter across all workloads' is not borne out by this page: sljit is slower than the interpreter on 27 of 108 queries (down to 0.81x on LIKE_3wild), median 1.11x (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: PostgreSQL 18.1; C/C++ compiler and build flags for pg_jitter, sljit and PostgreSQL not stated on the page. Benchmark script: tests/bench_comprehensive.sh in vladich/pg_jitter.
corrections.hardware: Apple M1 Pro, 32 GB RAM, Darwin 25.2.0 arm64
corrections.caveats: Indirect evidence: the numbers measure pg_jitter's sljit backend (pg_jitter's own code generator emitting through sljit), not the sljit library alone, and the sljit repo carries no benchmark of its own. pg_jitter's README tells users to build the patched fork vladich/sljit ('bug fixes, extra SIMD opcodes, memory management improvements'), so the measured code may not be upstream zherczeg/sljit. The harness runs llvmjit with jit_inline_above_cost=0 and jit_optimize_above_cost=0 (full LLVM inlining and optimization on every query) while the pg_jitter backends get 500000, which maximizes LLVM's compile time; PostgreSQL's defaults would skip LLVM optimization on cheap queries. With all thresholds at 0, LLVM compile cost dominates the end-to-end totals. Some LIKE/regex wins come from PCRE2 and StringZilla, not sljit codegen. Single machine, ARM64 only (x86_64 results 'TBD'), median of 3 runs, first-party pg_jitter numbers. The baseline is PostgreSQL's LLVM JIT, not one of the category baselines (PyPy, LuaJIT, V8, HotSpot).

notes: Numbers in the record are on the page and in the correct sljit column; the record's metric is compile-time, so I added the page's compile-overhead table (sljit 0.04-0.46 ms vs llvmjit 17-2043 ms) and flagged that the README's '5-25% faster than the interpreter across all workloads' claim is contradicted (sljit slower on 27 of 108 queries). Metadata checks out on github.com: 1.1k stars, BSD-2-Clause (Simplified BSD LICENSE file), not a fork, not archived, last commit 2026-09-30 (active). Main shortcomings: indirect evidence through pg_jitter, possibly the patched fork, and the LLVM side is forced to full optimization. sljit is not on an earlier wave's verified list (it was only mentioned as PCRE2's bundled JIT in wave 1), so this is not a duplicate; pg_jitter itself is a separate record in this wave.
